prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: sideswipe while changing lanes in Katy, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported wrist fracture. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1167; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The injury does not fit the crash: the impact was very light, yet the claimed injury is severe.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- Witnesses and the officer say the claimant was not in the vehicle when the crash happened.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: On a clear afternoon in Katy, Texas, Driver 1 was changing lanes when the front quarter of the vehicle contacted the rear quarter panel of Driver 2's vehicle, causing a sideswipe. Both vehicles were drivable and remained at the scene. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the policy. Officers reviewed scene photographs, which confirm the position of both vehicles and the general area of contact. The damage to both vehicles is consistent with the impact described by the drivers. Some older scratches appear on the affected panel, and it is not certain whether they predate this collision. No independent witnesses were located. Driver 2 and the responding officer both state that the Passenger was not inside the vehicle when the collision occurred. The Passenger later reported a wrist fracture. The impact appeared minor at the scene, and no airbag deployment was reported. Further medical records and statements will be needed to evaluate the reported injury.
